The journey & reference
groups.intro: How the user actually gets value, screen by screen, and which reference governs the build. The base reference is the engine's decoded Pinterest board library; a user-attached reference overrides it screen by screen once decoded.

purpose: The intake interview for the Pinterest UI Engine (v2). When a user starts the engine (see INTAKE.md), the AI opens with 'Hi, What are we building?', asks these questions, drafts product-brief.json using each question's briefPath, generates the full plan pack with engine/intake/make_plan.mjs, checks it with engine/intake/plan_doctor.mjs (which includes the brief doctor), shows the plan, and only builds after the user confirms. A question the user skips takes its default - but the default is a decision the AI states, never a silence.

questions.ask: What is the app called?
questions.why: The brand name heads every screen and names the app icon.

questions.ask: In one line, what does it do, and for whom? (e.g. 'Buy and sell pre-loved things near you.')
questions.why: Becomes the tagline and the About text the home and empty states speak in.

questions.ask: Which of these is it closest to?
questions.why: Selects the design world and the default vocabulary (listings, dishes, appointments…).

questions.ask: Where does it operate — city or region? And which currency?
questions.why: The header carries the place; money fields carry the currency.

questions.ask: What do you call ONE item in the catalogue — a product, a listing, a dish, a property?
questions.why: Every label in the app (search, tabs, empty states) uses this word.

questions.ask: Which facts does each item carry? Pick all that apply.
questions.why: These become the schema: facets feed filters and medallions, a rating feeds cards and the filter sheet, a second facet feeds the meta line.

questions.ask: Will items have real photographs?
questions.why: Photography is the board's colour. Without it the engine substitutes initials on tint — honest, but a different app.

questions.ask: Where do the items themselves come from?
questions.why: Real items make real screens; invented ones must be labelled samples.

questions.ask: How does buying work in this app?

options.label: Add to a bag/cart and check out
Book / reserve (pick a slot, then confirm)
No checkout — contact the seller / enquire

questions.why: A bag + checkout, a booking, or a contact-the-seller model are three different apps wearing one catalogue.

questions.ask: If there's a bag: what is it called on screen — Bag, Cart, Basket, Trolley?
questions.why: The tab, the empty state and the remove sheet all speak this word. (The requirement sentence keeps the trigger word 'cart' regardless.)

questions.ask: Can a buyer take more than one of the same item?

options.label: No — each item is one of one

questions.why: One-of-one catalogues (classifieds, one-offs) cap the bag at 1 and drop the stepper; stocked goods keep quantities.

questions.ask: What does checkout ask for, and in what shape?

options.label: Steps with delivery + payment as priced choices (the board's way)

questions.why: Declared as product.flow: radio rows for delivery/payment are the board's checkout; a parsed sentence only ever makes plain steps.

questions.ask: Is there a delivery fee? Free above some amount? (Skip for none.)
questions.why: Declared numbers — the bag's totals and the free-delivery line depend on them.

questions.ask: How should the home open?

options.label: Greeting header + category medallions (the board's home)

questions.why: The greeting header + category medallions is the board's home; the brand zone is the older composition.

questions.ask: Whose name greets on the home? (A demo user is fine — e.g. the app owner's own name.)
questions.why: The greeting header and the profile both need a person; an app without one ships with a hole in its first screen.

questions.ask: Which of the board's families should the app have? Pick any.

options.label: An offer card on the home

questions.why: Each picked family is declared in the brief and becomes working screens; each skipped one is absent — the engine never guesses them from prose.

questions.ask: If there's an offer card: what's the offer? (e.g. '30% — Get a discount for every order')
questions.why: The percent leads the card; a vague promo is the first thing that makes a generated home look generic.

questions.ask: Which look should it wear?

options.label: Auto — from the kind of app

questions.why: Mono is the board's own world (white, black, photography carries colour). Auto lets the domain decide.

questions.ask: Which reference should govern this build?

options.label: The base reference (the engine's decoded Pinterest board library)
My attached reference - decode it and build to it

questions.why: Base means every screen complies with the decoded board library. User means the attached reference is decoded first and governs the screens it covers; uncovered screens fall back to base. Recorded as referenceChoice: 'base' or 'user:<decode-id>' in the plan.

questions.ask: In your own words, what is the main thing a user does, start to finish? (e.g. 'Find a trusted sitter nearby, check reviews, book for Saturday, pay, then track the visit.')
questions.why: Becomes USER_JOURNEY.md's primary journey verbatim in spirit: every named step must resolve to a planned screen, or plan_doctor flags it. Prose journeys that never become screens are how thin apps happen.

questions.ask: Which screens must the app definitely have? Pick all that apply.
questions.why: Each picked screen is planned in DESIGN_DIRECTION.md and REFERENCE_PLAN.md with a governing reference type. Unpicked screens are only added when the journey or a declared family requires them - and the plan says why.

questions.ask: Does the app need booking - picking a date, time slot or appointment and confirming it?

options.label: Yes - request / enquire to book (no live slots)

questions.why: Booking is a different transaction than a bag: it plans the booking screen type (calendar/slot anatomy from the reference) and a booking flow in FUNCTIONALITY.md instead of, or alongside, checkout.

questions.ask: Does the app need chat or messaging between people in the app?

options.label: Contact only (call / WhatsApp / enquire button, no threads)

questions.why: Chat plans the chat screen type (thread list + conversation anatomy). Contact-only plans a contact action on detail instead - the engine is local-only, so chat is on-device threads, never a live messaging service; the plan must say so honestly.

questions.ask: Does the app need a wishlist / saved / favourites place?

options.label: Yes - heart/save toggle + a saved screen

questions.why: Wishlist plans the wishlist screen type and the save requirement sentence ('save ... with a heart toggle') that derives favourites. Without the sentence the toggle never appears.
